items.statement: On wards randomised to the tiered display, the proportion of high-severity interaction alerts with an appropriate response (accepted or appropriately overridden) is at least 9 percentage points higher than on standard-display wards over six months, without more harm from moderate interactions.
items.rationale: The retrieved trial suggests a large effect (c1), but contamination and a different outcome definition (c4) justify a conservative target; harm is a safeguard (c3).
items.risks: Contamination through rotation; pharmacist review workload.

items.statement: Interruptive alerts per 100 orders fall by at least half on tiered wards.
items.rationale: Volume reduction is consistent across studies.
items.risks: A process measure, not a benefit to patients.

items.statement: Tiering reduces reported prescriber alert burden.
items.rationale: Prescribers support tiering if high-severity alerts stay interruptive.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 is the primary comparison.
